correctness.rationale: Independently reproduced every size stratum and all five universality tests with /workspace/branches/replay_order16.py; read the submitted checkers but did not execute them. In the replay a pair of subsets of reciprocal sizes tiles iff its nonzero difference masks are disjoint: precisely such an intersection would give a repeated sum, and there are 16 sums. I grouped every zero-containing set of each divisor size by that difference mask, and intersected the exact Fourier-zero masks within each permissible complement bucket and then across permissible buckets. Evaluating in the basis 1,ζ,…,ζ^(E/2−1) with ζ^(E/2)=−1 gives the exact zero criterion (E=2 works too). Each possible spectrum translates to one containing 0; test its entire nonzero difference mask against the common Fourier-zero mask, checking all subgroups separately by difference closure. Translating complements changes each Fourier coefficient only by a phase, so no nonnormalized complement can change the mask. Uniformly over labeled tiles of size k, anchoring accounts for a fraction k/16, by double-counting a tile and a chosen element, also for periodic tiles. Replay produced totals (795,1611,2155,3147,4747) and obstruction totals (764,1056,1168,896,0), with all size columns as in RESULT.md. The cyclic example also checks: the alternating parity complements have all nonzero restricted character differences of {0,…,7} orthogonal, but difference 8 in the only order-eight dual subgroup restricts trivially. This proves the bounded order-16 classification; no extrapolation or formal proof claim.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The zero row in F2⁴ does have a short structural explanation: if A−A contains a subspace K of size |A|, then every complement is a transversal to K and K’s annihilator is universal. For sizes 2 and 4 take an included direction or the span of two independent directions in an anchored set of size 4; for size 8 the disjoint shifts are a nonzero coset b+Per(A) because all such shifts give the set complement of A, and a hyperplane can avoid that coset. Sizes 1 and 16 are immediate. This explains the contrast, rather than claiming a novel hard theorem in that group alone; it does not supply the non-elementary obstruction numbers.

evidence: Farkas–Matolcsi–Móra define one character basis shared by all complements; testing a clique in the intersection of Fourier zeros is the equivalent difference criterion. The cyclic framework uses universal spectra of a periodic form, not necessarily cosets.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: For a dual subgroup H, its restrictions are an orthogonal basis on B iff B is a transversal to H’s annihilator: Fourier coefficients on H record the occupancies of the quotient cosets. Requiring one such H for all B is stronger than individual spectrality or independent transversal choices. A frequency coset translates to H, and a universal spectrum which is itself a transversal of a subgroup need not be a subgroup coset.

value.rationale: A complete first comparably small multi-type cutoff for common Fourier bases tests a natural restriction: are simultaneous spectra still possible when the frequencies must form a subgroup coset? The exact profiles distinguish a common basis from a common quotient transversal, quantify how severely they diverge, and expose the elementary-abelian contrast, including abundant obstructions even in the cyclic group with prior existence. The value lies in the exact obstruction data across types, not in recomputing known tile counts.
